title: Inverse systems satisfying finite-cover lifting define site points
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site with finite limits. Let $(I,\geq,U_i,f_{ii'})$ be a directed inverse system of objects of $\mathcal C$: $I$ is a nonempty directed poset, each $i\geq i'$ has $f_{ii'}:U_i\to U_{i'}$, and $f_{ii}=\mathrm{id}$ and $f_{i'i''}f_{ii'}=f_{ii''}$. Define $u(W)=\varinjlim_{i\in I}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(U_i,W)$. Assume that for every covering family $\{W_k\to W\}_{k\in K}$ and every $f\in u(W)$ there are $k\in K$ and $g\in u(W_k)$ whose image in $u(W)$ is $f$. Then $u$ commutes with finite limits and sends every covering family to a jointly surjective family. Consequently $u$ is a point of the site in the sense of Tag 00YC (Proposition proposition-point-limits), and the point-to-topos construction of Tag 00YA (Lemma lemma-point-site-topos) gives a geometric morphism $p:\mathbf{Set}\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$ [def-trf-geometric-morphism] whose inverse image satisfies the canonical identification $p^{-1}\mathcal F\cong\varinjlim_{i\in I}\mathcal F(U_i)$ for every sheaf of sets $\mathcal F$.
